line_items.reasoning: NII came in at the upper half of the guided -7% to -9% range (now -8% to -9%), reflecting weaker loan balances and a surprise sweep deposit repricing headwind, but noninterest income surged 19% YoY, broadly offsetting the NII shortfall and sustaining the sixth consecutive quarter of YoY revenue growth — net result is roughly in line with the overall revenue outlook.

Q2 EPS of $1.33 grew sequentially from Q1's $1.20 and year-over-year, clearly exceeding the prior quarter's reaffirmed earnings outlook which carried a $0.06 FDIC drag and implied no meaningful improvement.

Full-year 2024 noninterest expense guidance was raised to ~$54B from the previously reaffirmed ~$52.6B, a ~$1.4B increase driven by elevated operating losses/customer remediation accruals, an additional FDIC special assessment, and higher WIM revenue-related compensation — a clear miss versus prior guidance.

Despite prior guidance that no step-up in the expense base was anticipated for CIB/trading investments, the overall expense base was raised materially to ~$54B, with higher WIM revenue-related comp and operating losses indicating the cost envelope expanded beyond what was guided.
